title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
hook: Interleave images and text in a prompt, use cross-attention to inject visual features into a frozen LLM, and get few-shot image understanding without retraining the language model.
key_points: Cross-attention layers inserted between frozen LLM blocks let visual features condition text generation without touching LLM weights.
A Perceiver Resampler compresses variable-length image or video features into a fixed number of visual tokens.
Few-shot prompting with image-text pairs transfers to new vision tasks, mimicking GPT-3-style in-context learning.
Trained on interleaved web image-text sequences, making it natural to handle multi-image and video inputs.
content_html: DeepMind's Flamingo, published in April 2022, introduced a practical way to give a powerful frozen language model visual perception without retraining it. Alayrac and colleagues trained new cross-attention layers and a Perceiver Resampler on top of existing LLM and vision encoder checkpoints, preserving the LLM's text capabilities while adding image and video understanding.
extra_html:
How it works

A vision encoder (similar in spirit to CLIP) processes each image or video clip into a set of features. A Perceiver Resampler then compresses those into a fixed number of visual tokens regardless of input resolution. These tokens enter the LLM via newly added cross-attention layers that sit between the frozen LLM's self-attention blocks. At inference, you can interleave multiple images and text examples in the prompt, and the model attends to the relevant visual context at each generation step.

Why it matters

Flamingo showed that in-context few-shot learning works for vision-language tasks, not just pure text, and that freezing a strong LLM while training lightweight bridge modules is a cost-effective strategy. That design pattern directly influenced later open models like LLaVA. Explore the details in the full paper on arXiv.

related.title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
related.hook: Connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM with just a linear projection, fine-tune on GPT-4-generated image dialogues, and get a capable open chat-with-images model for under a day of training.

related.title: In-Context Learning
related.hook: Paste a few examples into a prompt and a large language model performs the task - no gradient updates, no fine-tuning, the prompt is the program.
